title: Tom Pidcock wins Milano-Torino to underscore credentials ahead of Milan-Sanremo tilt
content:
Tom Pidcock soloed clear Primoz Roglic and Tobias Halland Johannessen in the final 600m of historic semi-classic Milan-Torino — his second victory of the season.

The 26-year-old’s performance also shows why the Briton is tipped as one of the only riders who may potentially upset favourites Tadej Pogacar and Mathieu van der Poel at Milan-San Remo.

Olympic mountain bike champion Pidcock is possibly the best descender in the peloton, which will likely help him on the climactic final descent of the Poggio on Saturday, but he used his climbing skills at Milan-Torino to burst away from a stacked field.

The group of favourites — which included Primoz Roglic, Tobias Johannessen, Giulio Pellizzari, and Cian Uijtdebroeks — were all together at the base of the Superga. Roglic was the first rider to attack, but Pidcock marked his move before counter-attacking relatively early.

His acceleration immediately separated him from the bunch, with Johannessen and Roglic never seriously looking as if they would close the gap.

Pidock won on debut by four seconds from Johannessen, with Roglic a further second back in third.

“Primoz is hard to read,” Pidcock said. “He is on the saddle all the time. I was expecting him to be good there. I hesitated to attack but eventually I did and the timing was right.”

Asked whether it demonstrated his form ahead of San Remo, Pidcock replied: “It shows I’m in good shape, but last year I was in really good shape, and I crashed at the bottom of the Cipressa.”

Elsewhere, Lidl-Trek ruled Italian sprinter Jonathan Milan has been ruled out of Milan-Sanremo with illness.

Though the race has traditionally been known as the “sprinters’ Monument”, that moniker has been shaken in recent years by more aggressive racing on the Cipressa and Poggio, which has led to just one victory from a pure sprinter since 2016.

Meanwhile, one of Milan’s sprint rivals, Jasper Philipsen won the Nokere Koerse race in Flanders on Wednesday afternoon, beating fellow Belgian Jordi Meeus into second place. Philipsen is also due to ride Milan-Sanremo on Saturday, and provides his Alpecin-Premier Tech team with a stellar alternative should Van der Poel suffer misfortune during the 300 kilometre race.
